greeting: Good morning, Rick! Happy Monday, here's a quick cup of tech news to start the week.

items.title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
items.note: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket failed minutes after liftoff from Florida on Sunday, taking 40 Amazon internet satellites down with it. It's the company's first total mission failure in 20 years and could ground the rocket for a while.

items.title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
items.note: Apple is inviting iPhone 15 and newer owners to join a study app that answers everyday health questions using trusted medical journals. It's a more careful take on asking a chatbot about your health.

items.title: Make iOS 27 Less Glassy and Siri Less Clingy With These Settings
items.note: If the see-through Liquid Glass look makes your iPhone harder to read, a quick setting can make it more solid. The guide also shows how to control what Siri saves and when video subtitles pop up.

items.title: AirPods Pro 3 hit Black Friday pricing early at $179 (Reg. $249)
items.note: Amazon dropped AirPods Pro 3 to $179, about $70 off and close to the lowest price ever. A nice early stocking stuffer if anyone on your list wants new earbuds.

items.title: Zoox robotaxis are now on the Uber app in Las Vegas
items.note: Amazon's boxy, driverless Zoox robotaxis can now be booked right in the Uber app in Las Vegas. Uber plans to add them in Los Angeles next year too.

items.title: How one 13-year-old is helping solve a huge solar panel limitation
items.note: Tired of moving his family's solar Christmas lights, a seventh grader built a water and gravity powered tracker that turns the panel toward the sun. It cost under $25 and made about 20 percent more power.

items.title: SNL gathers all the tech tycoons for a lesson in dating and spycraft
items.note: Saturday Night Live packed Musk, Zuckerberg, Altman and more into one sketch, with host John Mulaney as a CIA agent explaining why they should be suspicious of sudden admirers. Worth a look for a laugh.

items.title: No, the World Won't Shut Down on Nov. 17. What the Blackout Rumors Get Wrong
items.note: There's a nationwide Emergency Alert System test Tuesday around 1:20 PM Central, and social media is spinning it into doomsday rumors. Experts say it's just a routine test, so no need to worry.
